title: Nest Wifi shows solid orange light
shortDescription: The Nest Wifi point has lost internet connectivity.
fullDescription:
A solid orange (amber) LED on Google/Nest Wifi indicates the device can't reach the internet. This is most commonly a WAN-side issue such as a modem problem or an unplugged Ethernet cable on the primary router.

Mesh points will also show orange if they cannot reach the primary router.

fixSteps.title: Reboot modem and router
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug modem for 60 seconds, plug back in, then power-cycle Nest Wifi.

fixSteps.title: Check WAN cable
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat Ethernet between modem and Nest Wifi WAN (globe) port.

fixSteps.title: Contact ISP
fixSteps.instruction: If modem is fully online but router still orange, call ISP.

whenToCallPro: Call ISP if modem itself won't come online.
videoSearchQuery: Nest Wifi solid orange light fix

faq.a: Orange means no internet; red means hardware fault.

title: Nest Wifi point reported offline
shortDescription: A mesh point can't be reached by the primary router.
fullDescription: Google Home app lists the point as offline when the mesh backhaul fails or the point has lost power. Nearby clients will roam, but coverage in that area drops.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle point
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 30 seconds, reconnect, wait up to 2 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Move closer to primary
fixSteps.instruction: Position within 2 rooms of the primary router.

fixSteps.title: Run mesh test
fixSteps.instruction: Google Home app > Wifi > Test mesh and follow recommendations.

whenToCallPro: Contact Google support if point won't reconnect after factory reset.

faq.q: How do I run the mesh test?
faq.a: Google Home > Favorites > Wifi device > Test mesh.

title: Nest Wifi firmware update not completing
shortDescription: The firmware download or install stalls and doesn't finish.
fullDescription: Google Wifi updates run automatically and silently. Occasionally a stuck update will cause repeated LED flashing or a point to go offline during the process.

fixSteps.title: Check firmware version
fixSteps.instruction: Google Home > Wifi > Settings > Network check. Compare to current Google Wifi firmware.

fixSteps.title: Reboot entire network
fixSteps.instruction: Reboot primary then each point from the app or via power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset if frozen
fixSteps.instruction: If the primary won't update for over 48 hours, factory reset and set up again.

whenToCallPro: Contact Google support for orphaned firmware issues.

faq.a: No manual trigger – Google pushes updates silently; rebooting may prompt a retry.

title: Nest Wifi point lost connection to primary
shortDescription: Backhaul to the primary router has dropped.
fullDescription: Nest Wifi uses wireless backhaul between points and the primary. Interference, excessive distance, or firmware hiccups can break the link, leaving the point effectively isolated.

fixSteps.title: Run network check
fixSteps.instruction: Google Home > Wifi > Network check, follow relocation suggestion.

fixSteps.title: Relocate point
fixSteps.instruction: Place it between the primary and the dead zone, not beyond it.

whenToCallPro: Installer can run Ethernet backhaul for best results.
videoSearchQuery: Nest Wifi point mesh disconnect fix

faq.q: Does Nest Wifi support wired backhaul?
faq.a: Yes, Nest Wifi Pro supports wired backhaul between points.

title: Connected to Wi-Fi but no internet
shortDescription: SSID works but the router can't reach the internet.
fullDescription: Often caused by DNS issues, double-NAT with the ISP modem, or an IP lease problem after a WAN change.
symptoms: Works on modem directly but not Nest

fixSteps.title: Bridge ISP modem
fixSteps.instruction: Set ISP modem/gateway to bridge mode so Nest handles NAT.

fixSteps.title: Reboot chain
fixSteps.instruction: Modem first, then Nest Wifi primary. Wait for fully online between each.

fixSteps.title: Change DNS
fixSteps.instruction: Google Home > Wifi > Advanced networking > DNS > Custom (1.1.1.1).

whenToCallPro: ISP support for modem bridge mode.

faq.q: Can Nest Wifi Pro do multi-gig?
faq.a: Yes, Nest Wifi Pro supports 2 Gbps WAN speeds.

title: Google Home app cannot pair Nest Wifi
shortDescription: Setup fails at the QR code or Bluetooth scan stage.
fullDescription: Pairing issues usually come from QR code damage, missing permissions, or a point that wasn't factory reset.

causes.cause: Device still linked to previous Google account

symptoms: Factory reset doesn't re-enter setup mode

fixSteps.title: Enable permissions
fixSteps.instruction: Grant Location, Bluetooth, and Camera to Google Home app.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset on bottom for 10 seconds until LED flashes yellow.

fixSteps.title: Manual pairing
fixSteps.instruction: If QR fails, tap 'Enter setup key manually' on setup screen and input key printed under device.

whenToCallPro: Contact Google support for device-locked units.

faq.a: Printed under the device alongside the QR code.

title: Nest Wifi speeds below subscribed plan
shortDescription: Speedtest returns much less than ISP plan.
fullDescription: First-gen Google Wifi caps near 500 Mbps. Nest Wifi Pro supports Wi-Fi 6E and 2 Gbps WAN. Using an older unit on a gigabit plan will always under-perform.

causes.cause: Hardware limit on older Google Wifi

fixSteps.title: Wired baseline
fixSteps.instruction: Plug laptop into WAN-side of modem first; if slow there call ISP.

fixSteps.title: Force 5 GHz
fixSteps.instruction: Keep test client close and on 5 GHz.

fixSteps.title: Consider upgrade
fixSteps.instruction: For multi-gig plans, replace Google Wifi with Nest Wifi Pro.

whenToCallPro: Call ISP for line speed issues.

faq.a: Yes, Nest Wifi Pro supports 6 GHz band.

title: Sites won't resolve on Nest Wifi
shortDescription: Browsing fails but pings by IP work.
fullDescription: DNS issues are typically caused by an unreachable upstream resolver or incompatible custom DNS. Family Link filters can also block DNS lookups.

fixSteps.title: Revert DNS to automatic
fixSteps.instruction: Google Home > Wifi > Settings > Advanced networking > DNS > Automatic.

fixSteps.title: Check Family Link
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily disable filters for affected device.

whenToCallPro: Contact ISP for broader DNS issues.

faq.a: Nest Wifi Pro supports DNS over HTTPS when using custom DNS providers.

title: Nest Wifi hot and rebooting
shortDescription: Thermal events cause drops and reboots.
fullDescription: Passive cooling means placement matters. Enclosed spaces, media shelves, or direct sun can push the hardware past safe temperatures.

fixSteps.title: Relocate
fixSteps.instruction: Open shelf with airflow on all sides.

fixSteps.title: Clean vents
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out base vents with compressed air.

fixSteps.title: Replace if defective
fixSteps.instruction: If under warranty and overheating persists, request RMA.

whenToCallPro: Google support handles RMA for overheating units.

faq.a: Warm is fine; hot to touch plus random reboots is not.

title: Nest Wifi won't return to setup state
shortDescription: Factory reset doesn't put device in pairing mode.
fullDescription: Hold reset for 10 seconds until LED flashes yellow. If the device stays white/blue, the button may need a longer press or the device is locked to another account.
symptoms: Returns to white LED after release

fixSteps.title: Hold reset 10+ seconds
fixSteps.instruction: Press and hold until LED pulses yellow, release.

fixSteps.title: Unlink from prior Google account
fixSteps.instruction: Previous owner removes device from Google Home app.

fixSteps.title: Support for orphan devices
fixSteps.instruction: Proof of purchase to Google support required.

videoSearchQuery: Nest Wifi factory reset not working

faq.a: Yes – reset button bypasses the app for hardware reset.
